backlog.spec: Change UNCERTAIN_QUANTILE in infer.tta from 0.25 to 0.15 to cut prediction time at slight accuracy cost. Time saved should outweigh the accuracy loss if the TTA gain is concentrated in the least confident images.
backlog.title: Skip TTA second-stage fraction 0.25 -> 0.15

backlog.spec: In _get_tta_logits use only base_views = images_batch (no crop_tl/crop_br), so combined_inputs is original plus flipped (2 views). This cuts TTA compute by 3x. Keep the rest unchanged.
backlog.title: Drop shifted TTA views, keep flip only

backlog.spec: Set WHITEN_BIAS_EPOCHS = 0.1 so the whiten bias is frozen sooner. This slightly reduces backward work in early steps. Check for any accuracy effect.
backlog.title: Lower whitening-bias epochs to 0.1

backlog.spec: Change lr_factor2 from linear 1 - step/total to a shape of max(0, 1 - step/total)**1.2 for the Muon and head/bias groups. Use the same factor everywhere so the code stays simple.
backlog.title: Muon LR decay to nonzero floor shape: quadratic tail

backlog.spec: Multiply the lr_factor2 for the Muon group by min(1, (step+1)/10), a short linear warmup. This may allow slightly higher MUON_LR stability early.
backlog.title: Warmup of Muon LR over first 10 steps

backlog.spec: Set BATCH_SIZE = 2048, multiply MUON_LR by 1.15 and keep EPOCHS the same. Larger batches may improve GPU throughput. Watch accuracy.
backlog.title: Batch size 2048 with LR scaling

backlog.spec: Set BATCH_SIZE = 1024 and scale MUON_LR by 0.9 and HEAD_LR unchanged. More steps per epoch could allow reducing EPOCHS to 7.0 at the same accuracy.
backlog.title: Batch size 1024

backlog.spec: Set widths block2=224 and block3=224 (multiples of 32 for tensor cores). This reduces conv FLOPs by about 25 percent. Compensate with nothing initially and compare cost.
backlog.title: Reduce width of block2 and block3 to 224

backlog.spec: Set widths block1=96 while keeping the others. The early layer is cheap at low-res after pooling, so more capacity may raise accuracy, permitting fewer epochs.
backlog.title: Widen block1 to 96

backlog.spec: Replace nn.SiLU in ConvGroup with nn.GELU. The two are close and GELU may fuse differently under compile. Check cost.
backlog.title: Replace SiLU with GELU everywhere

backlog.spec: Leave the architecture but replace the final nn.MaxPool2d(3) by a global max pool via torch.amax over spatial dims (flatten), keeping the head input at 256 features. Simplifies and may differ slightly in accuracy.
backlog.title: Final pool MaxPool3 to adaptive max over 4x4

backlog.spec: In Conv.reset_parameters remove the dirac_ initialisation of the first channels so the init is plain default. Test whether the identity init is really helping.
backlog.title: Remove first-conv dirac init

backlog.spec: Set LABEL_SMOOTHING to 0.07 with all else equal. A small retune that may pair well with a short schedule.
backlog.title: Label smoothing 0.07

backlog.spec: Set the color_jitter enabled False in train aug. This removes two elementwise kernels per epoch and may lose little accuracy in a 7-epoch regime.
backlog.title: Disable color jitter

backlog.spec: Set TRANSLATE = 1 so less augmentation fits the short training. Check accuracy gain.
backlog.title: Translate 1 instead of 2

backlog.spec: For the first 40 percent of steps downsample batches to 24x24 with F.interpolate (bilinear, antialias off), then use full 32x32. Convs are fully convolutional and the final MaxPool(3) with floor handles sizes. Saves time in early steps.
backlog.title: Cutout-free random-resolution: train on progressive resolution

backlog.spec: Remove the third unrolled Newton-Schulz iteration in _zeropower_via_newtonschulz5, leaving two. This cuts optimizer time.
backlog.title: Muon Newton-Schulz with 2 iterations

backlog.spec: Set MUON_MOMENTUM = 0.70 and reduce MUON_LR to 0.195. Test whether smoother momentum helps.
backlog.title: Muon momentum 0.70

backlog.spec: Set HEAD_LR = 0.65 and BIAS_LR = 0.05. A small retune of the SGD groups.
backlog.title: Head LR higher, bias LR lower

backlog.spec: In Muon.step, set group['norm_freq'] = 8 constant instead of 2 + int(15*progress). Fewer norm computations per step.
backlog.title: Norm scaling frequency fixed at 8

backlog.spec: Set EPOCHS = 7.2 and MUON_LR = 0.215. Shorter training with slightly bigger steps; test if on the cost curve it beats baseline.
backlog.title: Epochs 7.2 with matching higher LR

backlog.spec: Change forward_step compile mode from 'max-autotune' to 'max-autotune-no-cudagraphs' (or default) and check whether per-run time changes. Compile is untimed.
backlog.title: Use max-autotune-no-cudagraphs for forward step

backlog.spec: In train, use train_loader.images[:480] instead of 960 for init_whiten. Slightly cheaper SVD and patch extraction.
backlog.title: Half-precision whitening init on fewer samples

backlog.spec: Perform batch_color_jitter on only the indexed batch (images[idxs]) rather than the full 50000 images per epoch, or conversely generate crop per batch. Compare time; reduces memory traffic for the final partial epoch (7.65 epochs means the last epoch is only 65 percent used).
backlog.title: Precompute all epoch augmentations less often

backlog.spec: In the loader __iter__, when it is the last epoch and only a fraction of steps will be used, still process only the needed indices: apply crop and jitter lazily on batches. Reduces wasted elementwise ops.
backlog.title: Skip augmentation work for unused final epoch fraction

backlog.spec: Set WEIGHT_DECAY = 0 so the foreach multiply is skipped entirely in Muon and SGD wd is zero. Simplifies code and saves a kernel per step.
backlog.title: Weight decay zero

backlog.spec: Set BatchNorm default momentum parameter (the value 0.5566) to 0.45 so running stats track recent weights better for the final model at test time.
backlog.title: BatchNorm momentum change

backlog.spec: Keep an EMA of conv weights updated every 2 steps in the last 30 percent of training with decay 0.9 using torch._foreach_lerp_, and swap into the model before predict by copying. Training LR goes to zero already, so test whether any gain exists; otherwise discard.
backlog.title: Ensemble-free EMA of weights over last steps

backlog.spec: Set nesterov=False in optimizer1 SGD construction. Quick check of simpler optimization for biases and head.
backlog.title: Nesterov off for SGD groups

backlog.spec: In train(), for the first ~40% of steps feed inputs downsampled to 24x24 (F.interpolate with mode='bilinear', antialias off, applied to each batch after indexing) and then switch to full 32x32 for the remainder. The network is fully convolutional up to the final MaxPool2d(3), so the head size stays valid if the final pool is replaced with adaptive max pooling to 1x1 (nn.AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1)); at 32x32 input the feature map is 4x4 -> the same as MaxPool(3) giving 1x1 so use adaptive pooling for both. Mark the shape change as one extra compile (shapes are fixed per phase; warm-up compile happens in the untimed first call). Keep total epochs the same or raise them slightly if accuracy drops.
backlog.title: Progressive resolution training

backlog.spec: In the tta() function, change _get_tta_logits so that it only uses images_batch and its flip (2 views instead of 6): base_views = images_batch; combined_inputs = torch.cat([images_batch, images_batch.flip(-1)]). This cuts TTA compute by 3x on the uncertain subset. Keep UNCERTAIN_QUANTILE at 0.25.
backlog.title: Drop the last TTA stage to flip-only on uncertain 25%

backlog.spec: Keep an exponential moving average (decay ~0.9) of all model parameters and BN running stats only during the last ~25% of training steps using torch._foreach_lerp_ on fp16 copies, then copy EMA into the model at the end of train(). Because LR decays to zero this may help little, so combine with a 5% reduction of EPOCHS (7.25) to trade for time. Use fused foreach ops to keep overhead low.
backlog.title: EMA of weights over final steps for evaluation

backlog.spec: Set widths to block1=64, block2=192, block3=192 in CifarNet and increase EPOCHS slightly (7.9). Smaller convs cut the dominant FLOPs by about 40 percent in blocks 2 and 3. Keep the Muon code unchanged (it pads to max dims automatically). Multiply MUON_LR by 1.1 to compensate for smaller filters.
backlog.title: Channels 256 to 192 in blocks 2 and 3 with higher Muon LR

backlog.spec: Make ConvGroup for block1 skip its second conv and norm (add a flag so block1 has conv1, pool, norm1, activ only) since block1 runs at the highest resolution (the 31x31 whitened input pooled to 15x15 only after conv1, so conv2 operates at 15x15 with 64 channels, cheap) — instead remove the second conv of block 2 at 256 channels ... Implement as: block2 keeps conv1 and conv2 but block1 drops conv2. Increase EPOCHS to 8.0 to compensate if accuracy drops. Remove the dirac init concerns: dirac_ init only applies when out>=in, which remains true.
backlog.title: Single-conv first block (remove conv2 in block1)

backlog.spec: Set BATCH_SIZE=2048, multiply MUON_LR, BIAS_LR and HEAD_LR by 1.15, and keep EPOCHS 7.65. Larger batches improve GPU utilisation and cut Muon optimizer overhead (fewer steps means fewer Newton-Schulz calls). Note len(train_loader) uses drop_last so 24 steps per epoch; verify total_train_steps is computed from it.
backlog.title: Batch size 2048 with sqrt LR scaling and fewer steps

backlog.spec: In _zeropower_via_newtonschulz5, delete the third unrolled Newton-Schulz iteration (keep two). Compensate by raising MUON_LR by 5 percent. This cuts matmul time in the optimizer, which is performed every step on padded 256x2304 stacks.
backlog.title: Cosine-free Muon with 2 Newton-Schulz iterations

backlog.spec: Set WHITEN_BIAS_EPOCHS to 0 behaviour: whiten_bias_grad always False (pass a constant False to forward_step so only one compiled graph is used and the whiten bias gradient is never computed), and remove the whiten bias from optimizer1 param groups. This removes a recompile-free but nonzero cost and simplifies code. Keep the bias at its initial zero value.
backlog.title: Lower-precision-friendly: skip whitening-bias training entirely

backlog.spec: Reduce LABEL_SMOOTHING to 0.05 and add a small L2 penalty on logits: loss = CE + 1e-4 * outputs.float().pow(2).mean(-1).sum() inside forward_step. The aim is the same calibration benefit with better fit in the short schedule, which can allow EPOCHS 7.4.
backlog.title: Label smoothing replaced by smaller smoothing plus mild mixup-free logit penalty

backlog.spec: Replace the reflect pad + gather-based batch_crop with a cheaper per-epoch approach: pick one random shift (dx,dy) in [-2,2] per group of 8 sub-batches... Simpler: generate per-epoch translated images using torch.roll on 5 random shift groups (split the 50000 images into 5 chunks by random permutation and roll each chunk by a different (dx,dy) in {-2..2}^2 using torch.roll). Roll wraps rather than reflects, which is acceptable at 2 pixels. This removes the advanced-indexing gather kernel, which is memory-bound on 50000x3x32x32.
backlog.title: Fused flip and translate in a single per-epoch pass without padded copy

backlog.spec: In infer()'s tta function, drop the shifted crop views (crop_tl, crop_br) in _get_tta_logits so base_views is just images_batch, and combined_inputs is [images_batch, images_batch.flip(-1)]. This cuts TTA compute by 3x on the uncertain quarter. Keep everything else unchanged. Averaging then covers 2 views.
backlog.title: Skip TTA views: flip-only on uncertain 25%

backlog.spec: Change UNCERTAIN_QUANTILE from 0.25 to 0.15 in infer() tta function. This reduces predict time at a small accuracy cost; check net cost.
backlog.title: Reduce TTA uncertain fraction to 0.15

backlog.spec: Set BATCH_SIZE = 2048, multiply MUON_LR, BIAS_LR and HEAD_LR by 1.15 (roughly sqrt of 4/3), keep EPOCHS the same. Larger batches improve GPU utilization and reduce per-step optimizer overhead (Muon Newton-Schulz runs fewer times). WEIGHT_DECAY scaling is automatic via wd = WEIGHT_DECAY*batch.
backlog.title: Batch size 2048 with LR scaling

backlog.spec: In _zeropower_via_newtonschulz5, delete the third unrolled iteration block (the last A = X @ X.transpose; B = ...; X = a*X + B@X) so only 2 NS iterations run. Reduces optimizer time per step; orthogonalization is looser but coefficients are tuned to be aggressive.
backlog.title: Newton-Schulz with 2 iterations

backlog.spec: Change the downsample in the training loop to size (20, 20) rather than 24x24 for step < 0.3*total_train_steps. Note compile uses fixed shapes: this yields only two shapes so recompiles happen once in warmup (untimed). Speeds early steps further. Make sure the dynamo recompile does not break: shapes are static since automatic_dynamic_shapes is False.
backlog.title: Low-res phase for first 40% at 20x20 then 32

backlog.spec: Set WHITEN_BIAS_EPOCHS = 0.0 effectively by making whiten_bias_grad always False (pass False constant) and removing the whiten bias param group from the optimizer. This removes a compile variant and the extra gradient work in early steps.
backlog.title: Skip whitening-bias training

backlog.spec: Set LABEL_SMOOTHING = 0.07 and WEIGHT_DECAY = 0.0. With very short training, regularization is probably unneeded; may gain accuracy for free.
backlog.title: Label smoothing 0.07 with wd zero

backlog.spec: Replace nn.AdaptiveMaxPool1(1) at the end of layers by AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) followed by nothing but instead add an extra average-pool mix: x = 0.5*(AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1)(x) + AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1)(x)) in a small module. Cheap change that may give accuracy gain from richer pooling.
backlog.title: Final pool: adaptive max over 2x2 then mean

backlog.spec: In ConvGroup for the first block, drop conv2/norm2/activ so block1 has only conv1, pool, norm1, activ (add a flag single=True to ConvGroup used only for block1). Output channels remain 64 so the next block is unchanged. Block1 runs on the highest resolution, so this saves substantial time; compensate with EPOCHS 8.0 if needed.
backlog.title: Single conv in block1

backlog.spec: Set the SGD optimizer1 nesterov=False (momentum 0.825 kept), and in Muon.step replace the schedule group['norm_freq'] = 2 + int(15*progress) with a constant 8. Simplifies code and removes some per-step overhead from foreach_norm calls.
backlog.title: Remove nesterov in SGD and set Muon norm_freq fixed

incumbent.description: Pass the per-step target magnitude as a tensor instead of the Python int step count, so the compiled Newton-Schulz function is not recompiled every step and no longer hits the cache size limit.

memo: Only one change helped: slot 8, passing the per-step target magnitude as a tensor instead of a Python int (-0.0935 official). It looks like a compile or overhead fix, not a model change. Everything else was rejected. That covers removing the dirac init (+0.0567), disabling jitter (+0.0555), per-batch jitter (+0.0304), narrower widths (+0.0697), roll-based crop (+0.0731), EMA (+0.0205 vs incumbent), GELU (+0.0620) and dropping a Newton-Schulz iteration (+0.3895). TRANSLATE=1 (-0.1290/-0.1150 over 2 runs) and HEAD_LR 0.65 / BIAS_LR 0.05 (-0.0343/-0.0031) were also rejected, but each scored better than the incumbent in at least one run. Progressive resizing crashed once, and the 20x20 variant did not beat the incumbent. Next: replicate TRANSLATE=1 and the HEAD_LR/BIAS_LR retune on top of slot 8, since the noise sd is about 0.026. Then look for other overhead wins, such as Python scalars that cause recompiles or syncs, a lighter data pipeline, and cheaper test-time augmentation. Avoid architecture shrinking and removing augmentation.
